acceptance: The guard and the primary-clone check use the override only when it resolves to a worktree listed by git worktree list for the repository being checked; otherwise they fall back to the common directory's parent. A unit test shows a stray override pointing at an unrelated repository no longer lets a relative write into the real primary clone through.

agent_write_preflight.sh either applies the same rule or keeps its current behaviour with a recorded reason; its tests that point the override at an unrelated directory (_run_preflight in tests/unit/test_agent_write_preflight.py) are updated to build a matching worktree layout rather than weakened.
Existing tests in tests/unit/test_primary_clone_write_guard.py and tests/unit/test_agent_write_preflight.py pass.
Decision gate: none needed if the rule above is kept; any alternative, such as removing the override and using another test seam, needs the owner's approval first.

Guardrails: BENCHBOX_ALLOW_MAIN_CLONE_WRITE=1 still bypasses; the omp hook module is not changed unless its pinned digest in _project/scripts/agent_instruction_audit.py is updated in the same change; no probe writes are left in the primary clone.
description: scripts/primary_clone_write_guard.py, scripts/check_primary_clone_clean.sh and scripts/agent_write_preflight.sh all take the primary clone from BENCHBOX_AGENT_PRIMARY_CLONE when it is set, and trust it without checking it. The variable exists so tests can point the scripts at a scratch repository. On 2026-11-17 it was left exported in an agent shell after a timing test, and claude -p sessions started from that shell inherited it: the hook then treated the scratch repository as the primary clone, and a Write and an Edit landed in the real primary clone (both reverted at once). The preflight backstop reads the same variable, so it would not have reported them either. docs/agent/primary-clone-guard.md warns against leaving it set; nothing enforces that.
